title: The Lull
version: FINAL storyboard v1.0 (astronaut; comedy base + the three judges' grafts), 2026-10-23, storyboard only, for Alex's review
status: storyboard only: no image, video or audio generated; no network; for Alex's review
logline: Mid-spacewalk, an astronaut gets Marketing's email: the launch moved up, the film is due tonight. With five deadpan prompts from her wrist display she has Manus 2.0 recast every disaster that follows (a tether that runs out, a debris shower in a solar storm, an airlock that will not seal, a fireball re-entry) as a serene launch film for the station's new guest module, and it ships while she is in radio blackout. Then, bobbing on the ocean, she gets the next brief.

engine.ours: Space-disaster film (the Gravity / Apollo 13 register), played straight by the camera, the grade and the danger.

engine.part: Running joke: a desk job inside an action movie
engine.hf01: he calmly opens a laptop while an arrow thunks above his head
engine.ours: every loop she gives a calm creative note about the disaster happening to her, and the film she is making recasts it as luxury: her drift becomes the serene opener, debris becomes shooting stars, the radiation alarm becomes mood lighting, the re-entry fire becomes the ending. One rule, set by P1 ('Make it calm.'), that the audience learns and then watches every disaster test.

engine.part: A set piece in every loop, escalating
engine.hf01: waterfall, monkeys on a rope bridge, the arrow, the temple boulder
engine.ours: an orbital sunrise blast -> her tether runs out and snaps taut -> a debris shower chases her along the truss over an aurora as a solar storm arrives -> trapped in an airlock that will not seal, radiation alarm, the wrench she lost this morning comes back an inch above her helmet -> re-entry fireball and radio blackout (the peak).

engine.hf01: 'What is it this time? Objects? Shapes? VFX?', a shouted 'The easy route!'
engine.ours: zero-G floating words that literally drift and turn: 'Tonight?' 'From space?' 'Nose itches.' 'Sunrise. Again.' 'Deep breath.' 'Not that deep.'; a delighted shout under the debris: 'Wish fast!'

engine.part: The deliverable is about her world
engine.hf01: a promo for the very reserve he is crossing
engine.ours: the launch film for The Lull, the station's new guest module ('the quietest room in orbit'), cut from her own helmet-cam footage of the day going wrong.

engine.part: A punchline ending; the loop starts again
engine.hf01: 'Looks great! Next brief: a safety video for the reserve.'
engine.ours: splashdown: 'Booked solid.' then a follow-up, 'Undersea next?', while she sits on the capsule in the open sea. She looks down at the water. A gull lands as the music stops.

world.setting: One working day on a fictional, unbranded orbital station (working name Arden Station, never on screen): white modules in matte white and pale-gold insulation blankets, a long open lattice truss with white handrails, blue-black solar arrays, a small white re-entry capsule (one orange band) docked at a port, and the new guest module, The Lull: a soft, rounded white module with one large round window. Then that capsule's re-entry and the open ocean at golden hour. No real agency's or company's names, flags, logos or insignia; no hardware that copies a real station's signature parts (BANNED_WORLD below lists them for the build check; no generation prompt names them); our own text-free mission patch only.
world.never: hf01's world (jungle, waterfall, rope bridge, fire, ruins, arrow, temple, cave, stone sphere) and Manus's plates (waterfall, glacier canyon, salt flat, rock spires, dunes, dumpling shop, shophouse street). Listed here for people and for the build check only, never inside a generation prompt.
world.astronaut: Commander Wren Adair (fictional; her name is never on screen; CAST.md).
world.sender: Marketing (the station operator's ground marketing team; only the word 'Marketing' is ever shown).
world.deliverable: The Lull, a 30 s launch film for the station's new guest module (a product ad, F9), 16:9.
world.clock: Station time: the email at 09:12; the countdown T–09:48:00 runs to 19:00, Marketing's deadline and, as a capsule glyph beside it hints (S04), about when her capsule comes home; re-entry and blackout ~18:40 (S24); the reply at 19:47, on the sea (S26).
escalation: S01-S04 loop 1: the email mid-spacewalk; the wrench drifts off her glove (she lets it go); the bag will not drop; an orbital sunrise blasts her visor.

S09 loop 2: she drifts off the hull with her tether paying out behind her; she art-directs it (P2); the tether runs out and snaps taut, yanking her out of frame. Tethered, so nobody is lost: comic peril.

S14-S15 loop 3: night side over an aurora, a solar storm arriving (sensor sparkle, the helmet caution lamp); a debris shower chases her hand over hand along the truss (P3: call it shooting stars; 'Wish fast!').

S20-S22 loop 4: the storm forces her inside; the airlock will not seal (her tether is caught in the outer hatch); the radiation alarm pulses red; the wrench she lost at 09:12 comes back around and clangs off the rim an inch above her helmet (P4: mood lighting). Trapped, irradiated, nearly hit: worse than loop 3.
S24 loop 5, the peak: re-entry; plasma fire in the window, the cabin shaking, the signal dropping bar by bar; P5 goes out on the last bar, then loss of signal. The job finishes without her (S25).
S26 the release: splashdown at golden hour; the reply and the next brief.

early_payoff: Two beats before the film's midpoint, so the joke pays off on screen early. (1) S13 n1063-1086 (35.4-36.2 s): her drift plays in the viewer at half speed under 'Breathe easy.': the most alarming moment of her morning is now the calm opener. (2) S17 n1294-1361 (43.1-45.4 s): the debris she was ducking plays slowed and warm as shooting stars under 'Wish slowly.', the spa-ad version of what she shouted 4 s earlier ('Wish fast!'). hf01's playhead never moves; ours moves only in these two shots.

jokes.joke: Her long deadpan stare at an email from Marketing, 400 km up; 'Launch moved up.' read by someone already up; the wrench simply leaves her glove and she does not look.
The pack drop in zero G: she lets go of the bag and it just stays there. The thud never comes.
Floating thoughts: 'Tonight?' 'From space?' 'Nose itches.' (the helmet glyph gets bonked) 'Sunrise. Again.' 'Deep breath.' 'Not that deep.'
'Alarms: muted' in loop 1, before anything has gone wrong (second viewing).
Drifting off the station, she art-directs it ('Open on this drift.'); then the tether runs out and yanks her out of frame.
'Drift first.': her near-miss, filed as shot one.
Her drift plays as a spa ad under 'Breathe easy.'
Under a debris shower in a solar storm: 'Call it shooting stars.' then a delighted 'Wish fast!'
'Debris → stars.' Then the debris plays slowed and warm as shooting stars under 'Wish slowly.'
'Adding whale song…' to a space spa film.
'Loose items leave.' in the film's own house rules, 2.6 s before one comes back.
The wrench she lost at 09:12 comes back around and clangs off the rim an inch above her helmet; she watches it go; 'Red alarm? Mood lighting.'
'Mood lighting included.' sold in a red pill.
In a re-entry fireball, signal dying: 'End on this glow. Ship it.' The plush whale swings.
'No signal' cuts straight to a blue check: shipped while she was unreachable.
'Booked solid.' then 'Undersea next?' She looks down at the sea she is sitting on. Pull back: a lot of sea. The music stops; a gull lands.
'Out of office. / Out of range. / Still shipping.'

kit.grade_and_cadence: Animate and cut on a 24 fps master and map to 30 fps by index (out[n] = master[m(n)], m(n) = 12*(n//15) + r - [r>=5] - [r>=10] - [r>=14], r = n % 15), so every cut and judder step lands on hf01's frame (gaps/footage.md items 16-17: a build task; the skill renders 60 fps). Delivery 1920x1080.
kit.brand_rules: Off-white #F7F7F7 grounds with a faint 16 px dot grid; ink #1F1F1F (#1D2126 over bright plates, white with a soft dark halo over space); one sky-blue #33ABFB on at most one word per card, #2CB4F3 on line icons and the progress hairline; Inter for all UI and claims; serif only inside the Manus wordmark file; colour lives in the footage and in the ad, never in our UI. Logos only from manus2/brand/: manus-mark-dark.svg, manus-wordmark-dark.svg, the -white versions, manus-app-icon.svg (the plain .svg files render blank). The mark never rotates, morphs or acts as a character. No status card goes whole-line blue. The title card carries one blue accent only (the unread dot).
kit.reading_rule: Every string is timed from the frame it becomes legible (r) to its last frame (l). A string may carry at most 3.0 words per readable second, and so may every group of strings read together (strings whose legible windows overlap share one span, first r to last l). Every word on screen counts: labels, repeats and the sender too. Words are whitespace tokens; '·', '/', '→' and '…' are not words; a timecode or file name is one word; logos are not counted. build.py fails the build above 3.0.

kit.score: Style B (the ridge's decision table): bright F major on hf01's 87.01 BPM grid (first beat 0.1107 s), every sync point kept: unpulsed to n665; groove in on bar 8 at n665.3 (+144 ms after the S05 cut); break (low end out) n1402.5; bar 18 back n1492.8; drop 1 n1658.3 (+244 ms after n1651; 808 pickup ~80 ms before the cut); drums thin on bar 22 n1823.8; drop 2 n1906.6; groove stops on bar 25 n2072 (the gull lands on it); digital silence n2170-2186; sting n2186 (0.368 s after n2175). The vacuum rule, in order: space is silent, so S01-S22 carry only in-suit sound (breath, suit fans, radio chirps, contact sounds through the suit: the thud that never comes S02, the visor bonk S04, the tether twang S09, the wrench knock S22); the re-entry roar through the hull (S24) is the film's first loud real sound; the waves at splashdown (S26) are its first natural sound.
